sourcedFrom: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) (2026 (© 2026, Samsun Yurt Savunma Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş.))
cleanIntro: ⛔ THIS IS THE STEEL-FRAMED RIVAL-S AND IT DOES NOT SHARE PARTS WITH THE RIVAL. At 1210 g with an empty magazine against the RIVAL's 835 g the difference is not subtle, and neither is the consequence of mixing a bench full of parts — a steel-framed pistol will still close on the wrong barrel. If both guns are in the house, keep their parts apart before either one comes open. ⚠ Eye protection before anything opens: springs are under tension in here and solvents fly. Work with the pistol supported on your lap or a table rather than in mid-air — the strip needs both hands doing different jobs at the same moment. ⛔ Threaded muzzle protector off before disassembly.

steps.title: Magazine out first — and this pistol fires with the magazine removed
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction. Hold the pistol in one hand, press the magazine release with your thumb and let the magazine fall into your free hand.
steps.prose: Magazine, then chamber, then striker. That is the book's own order and the reason for it is in the warning.
steps.quote: 1. While keeping the pistol pointed in a safe direction, hold the pistol with one hand, depress the magazine release button with your thumb and the magazine should fall into your free hand.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Unloading the Pistol, printed p.15
steps.warn: WARNING! The pistol will fire if the magazine is removed and if the trigger is pulled when a cartridge is in the chamber.

steps.title: Chamber checked twice — by eye and by finger
steps.action: Grasp the slide under the rear sight, run it fully rearward and hold it open, and inspect the chamber. Then cycle the slide AGAIN and check it a second time, visually and by feel with your little finger.
steps.prose: The second cycle is the part people skip. One look into a dark chamber is not a check.
steps.caution: Look AND feel. A brass case head in shadow reads as an empty chamber.
steps.quote: 2. Grasp the slide under the rear sight and move it fully rearward, holding the slide fully open inspect the chamber to ensure it is empty.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Unloading the Pistol, printed p.15

steps.title: Striker down, and the red indicator is how you know
steps.action: Let the slide go forward on the empty chamber, then — muzzle still safe — pull the trigger to lower the striker.
steps.prose: ⛔ The strip does not begin until this is done. A visible tell for striker state is unusual and worth using every time rather than trusting the trigger pull you think you just made.
steps.caution: Red showing = striker still cocked. No red = down.
steps.quote: 3. Allow the slide to go forward on the empty chamber. While pointing the pistol in a safe direction pull the trigger to lower the striker.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Unloading the Pistol, printed p.15

steps.title: Both take-down catches DOWN while the slide goes forward 0.6 inch
steps.action: Grasp the take down catches above the trigger and pull them DOWN with the index finger and thumb of your secondary hand while pushing the slide FORWARD with the thumb of your primary hand. At about 0.6 inch, lift the slide up and off the frame.
steps.prose: Two hands, two directions, at the same moment. ⚠ 0.6 inch is the whole travel, not a false stop — if the slide will not go, one of the catches is not fully down. This is a both-sides part.
steps.caution: 0.6 inch forward is the full travel. Lift the slide off at that point; do not force it further forward.
steps.quote: 2. While holding the pistol in your primary hand, grasp the take down catches, located above the trigger. Pull them down using index finger and thumb of your secondary hand.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Field Stripping, printed p.16

steps.title: Recoil spring — push it toward the MUZZLE, then lift it out
steps.action: Hold the slide in your primary hand and, with the secondary hand, push the recoil spring TOWARD THE MUZZLE and lift it free. It comes out forward-then-up, not straight up.
steps.prose: Compressing it slightly is what releases it from its seat. Trying to lift it straight out binds it against the front of the slide.
steps.quote: 1. Holding the slide with primary hand, use your secondary hand to push the recoil spring toward the muzzle and lift it free.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Disassembly, printed p.17

steps.title: Bore from the CHAMBER to the muzzle, nylon brush and CLP
steps.action: Attach the correct-calibre nylon bore brush to the rod, dampen it with CLP and push/pull it through the barrel several times FROM THE CHAMBER TO THE MUZZLE.
steps.prose: Chamber-to-muzzle carries fouling out of the barrel rather than back over the chamber mouth.
steps.quote: 4. Dampen the screw-in nylon bore brush with cleaner, lubricant, protectant (CLP) and then push/pull the brush through the barrel several times from the chamber to the muzzle.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.32

steps.title: Patch until it comes out clean — that is the finish line, not a count
steps.action: Repeat brush-and-patch until a final patch comes out clean after swabbing the bore, then leave a light coat of CLP in the bore.
steps.prose: A condition, not a number of passes. For a high-volume shooter that is the difference between a five-minute clean and a fifteen-minute one, and the barrel decides which.
steps.quote: 6. Repeat this process with the brush and cleaning patches until a final patch comes out clean after swabbing the bore. Apply a light coating of CLP to the bore of the barrel.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.32

steps.title: ⛔ Nothing more abrasive than Scotch Brite, ever
steps.action: Keep anything more abrasive than Scotch Brite away from every part of the pistol and the suppressor — no sandpaper, no emery cloth. Use solvents only in a well-ventilated area away from open flames.
steps.prose: The surfaces this protects are the same rails and lugs the CLP list names. Once they are scratched, no amount of lubricant puts them back.
steps.caution: Scotch Brite is the ceiling. Sandpaper and emery cloth are out.
steps.quote: Abrasives more aggressive than Scotch Brite may damage the precision contact surfaces of the pistol, resulting in friction that can lead to malfunctions of the firearm and suppressor.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and Maintenance — MAINTAINING THE FINISH ON YOUR PISTOL, printed p.32

steps.title: CLP goes on FIVE named places and nowhere else
steps.action: Take the shooting residue off the slide, the barrel's exterior and the action parts with the supplied brush and cloth. Then a LIGHT coat of CLP on: the rails, the trigger bar, the inside of the ejector assembly of the frame, the rails on the slide and the firing pin block, together with the slide's inner side where the barrel operates.
steps.prose: That list is precise and it is short. Everything not on it gets residue removed and no oil added — which on a striker pistol is the point.
steps.quote: 7. Remove shooting residue from the slide, barrel's exterior, and action parts using the brush and cloth supplied. Apply a light coating of CLP to the rails, trigger bar and inside of the ejector assembly of frame and rails on the slide and firing pin block together with the slide's inner side where the barrel operates.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Cleaning and Maintenance, printed p.32

steps.title: Barrel back in first — muzzle-DOWN, then turn it UP
steps.action: Hold the slide muzzle-DOWN and drop the barrel in; turn the slide muzzle-UP and the barrel falls into place.
steps.prose: Gravity does the barrel for you if you turn the slide over instead of fighting it.
steps.quote: 1. Hold the slide in your primary hand with the muzzle side facing the ground. Drop the barrel into the slide, turn the slide up so that the muzzle now is facing the sky.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Reassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: Recoil spring in — ⛔ FLAT END toward the CHAMBER
steps.action: Place the recoil spring in the muzzle end of the slide with the FLAT END facing the chamber, pressing it toward the muzzle and slightly down with the thumb of your secondary hand.
steps.prose: This is the detail that gets reversed. Check which end is flat before it goes in.
steps.caution: Flat end of the recoil spring toward the CHAMBER.
steps.quote: 2. While holding the slide in your primary hand, place the recoil spring in the muzzle end of the slide.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Reassembly, printed p.18

steps.title: Slide on 0.6 inch from the rear, then pushed rearward
steps.action: Align the slide cutouts with the frame rails, press the slide onto the frame about 0.6 inch from the rear, and push it rearward until both take-down catches spring back up flush.
steps.prose: Only this gun's parts go back into this gun.
steps.quote: 3. Align the slide cutouts with frame rails. Press slide onto the frame which is about 0.6" distance from the rear. Push the slide rearward.
steps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Reassembly, printed p.18

deepSteps.title: Lubrication · the bore
deepSteps.gloss: The coat you leave in the bore at the end of a clean is exactly the material this passage is about. Leave it for storage; take it out before shooting.
deepSteps.quote: Firing a firearm with oil, grease or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the firearm and injury to the shooter and those nearby.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Lubrication Warning, printed p.33

deepSteps.title: Lubrication · ammunition
deepSteps.gloss: The squib chain, from the cause end: lubricant reaches the powder, the powder does not ignite, the primer alone seats the bullet in the bore, and the round after it does the damage.
deepSteps.quote: Do not spray or apply lubricants directly on ammunition.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Lubrication Warning, printed p.33

deepSteps.title: Alterations · aftermarket parts
deepSteps.gloss: On a competition pistol this is the passage most likely to matter, because these are the guns people modify. A warranty consequence is the maker's claim by nature and cannot be paraphrased into ours.
deepSteps.quote: Installation of anything other than a CANiK Accessory Program part will void the pistol warranty and may result in damage to the pistol or injury or death.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Warning Concerning Alterations and Aftermarket Parts!, printed p.33

deepSteps.title: Storage
deepSteps.gloss: The book puts the bore check on the way OUT of storage rather than on the way in — which is the right end, because that is when it matters.
deepSteps.quote: Your pistol should be thoroughly cleaned and lightly lubricated before being put away for storage. A light coating of good quality gun oil should be applied to all exposed surfaces.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Storage, printed p.35

deepSteps.title: Finish · the barrel
deepSteps.gloss: Worth reading before you see the wear and assume something is wrong. Reproduced as printed, including “gun oil of CLP”.
deepSteps.quote: NOTICE: Like all firearm finishes, the PVD treatment on your barrel will wear with repeated use. Keeping the barrel lubricated with a recommended gun oil of CLP will provide the longest durability and corrosion resistance.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Lubrication Warning — NOTICE, printed p.33

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Suppressor OFF before the pistol is opened — not after
deepSteps.action: Assembly and disassembly of the pistol or the suppressor must NEVER be performed while the suppressor is fitted. Remove it completely, open the action, confirm the pistol is unloaded and the chamber empty, then work on either one.
deepSteps.prose: The moment this is written for is wiping a can down with the pistol still hanging off it.
deepSteps.quote: Always completely remove the suppressor from the firearm before assembly and/or
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Suppressor Ready Models — WARNING! 5: SUPPRESSOR MAINTENANCE, printed p.28

deepSteps.title: Thread protector · scope of the section
deepSteps.gloss: This is the only verbatim line the corpus holds for that section. The useful fact — that the metric barrel is a LEFT-HAND thread — is carried in the walk in our voice, because no sentence on file states it in Canik's.
deepSteps.quote: Notice! This section only applies to threaded barrel configurations.
deepSteps.cite: CANiK SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual — SFx RIVAL-S Owner's Manual (no form code printed) — Removing and Installing the Thread Protector, printed p.31

tasks: Patch until a patch comes out CLEAN
Light CLP coat left in the bore
⛔ Dry patch it out before the next round is fired

cleaning.name: CLP — THE FIVE NAMED PLACES
tasks: Inside of the ejector assembly of the frame
Rails on the slide and the firing pin block
The slide's inner side where the barrel operates

cleaning.name: ⛔ PARTS DISCIPLINE
tasks: Barrel and some other components DO NOT interchange with an SFx RIVAL
One pistol on the bench at a time if you own both
Rebuild from the parts that came off THIS gun

cleaning.name: THREADED MUZZLE / SUPPRESSOR
tasks: ⛔ Suppressor completely removed before any assembly or disassembly
⛔ Factory-new JACKETED ammunition only with a can fitted

reassembly: Slide muzzle-DOWN, barrel dropped in; turn muzzle-UP and it seats.
⛔ Recoil spring FLAT END toward the CHAMBER.
Slide on about 0.6 inch from the rear, then pushed rearward.
⛔ THIS gun's barrel and components only — they do not interchange with an SFx RIVAL.
Threaded muzzle protector back on with the supplied wrench, if fitted.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber clear, suppressor off. Cycle the slide full travel and confirm it returns fully into battery with both take-down catches sprung back up flush. Work the ambidextrous slide stop from both sides. Dry-fire on the empty chamber and watch the red striker indicator go out and return on the next cycle. ⛔ Before any of that, satisfy yourself the barrel in the gun is THIS gun's barrel. Then dry-patch the bore.
